relevance_note: Multicentre French paediatric-onset HA20 cohort that describes its 17 TNFAIP3-variant carriers individually by number, e.g. "Patient 6 experienced recurrent fever, oral and genital ulcers and autoimmune hepatitis", with per-patient variants in Table 3.
method_note:
Read the whole paper, then typed every value into a Python builder script in my scratch directory. The script looks each span up in the paper (a space in a typed quote may match a thin space in the paper) and stops if a quote is missing. I transcribed the Table 3 rows into the script by hand and checked them cell by cell against the table. Table 3 prints ranges ("Patient 1–3", "Patient 10–13"), which I expanded to patients 1, 2, 3 and 10, 11, 12, 13 (same family, same variant). Labels use the paper's most frequent form, "patient N" (lowercase: 36 uses against 18 capitalised).

SCOPE: the 17 cohort patients, who all carry a TNFAIP3 variant, plus the relatives the text describes in families 2 and 8.

POSSIBLE DUPLICATES, NOT MERGED: Table 3 puts patients 10–13 in family 8. The text describes patient 10's half-brother, half-sister, mother and maternal grandfather but never maps them to patients 11–13. Some of them, probably the half-brother, half-sister and mother, are likely the same people as patients 11–13: the mother's uveitis matches patient 12, the only stated case of ocular involvement. I kept them as separate rows; reconciliation should check.

FAMILY 2 RELATIVES: I read "aunt and two nieces of the grandfather" literally, as relatives of patient 4's grandfather; whose aunt she is remains ambiguous. Their features ("recurrent ulcers and chronic hepatitis") are stated only for the three together, so I did not assign them to any one person. The paper gives no related person for "another cousin", so that row is labelled "unnamed person 1".

NO VARIANT ROWS FOR RELATIVES: the paper reports heterogeneity "even among relatives carrying identical TNFAIP3 mutations" and uses families 2 and 8 as examples, but never states a genotype for an individual relative. The supplementary pedigree text marks at least one family 2 relative "(not tested)".

SUPPLEMENT: the converted text of supplementary figures 1 and 2 has lost its layout and patient labels (the timelines carry no labels and the pedigree text is jumbled), so I took no per-person values from them. Supplementary tables 1a–1c are excerpts with no data rows. Supplementary figure 2 shows "Uveitis" in two different timelines, while the main text states ocular involvement in only one patient (patient 12); the timelines cannot be mapped to patients.

GROUP STATEMENTS NOT EXPANDED: these were not turned into per-person excluded rows: colitis "in 6/17 patients" with six patients named; "No patient fulfilled the clinical or biological criteria for connective tissue disease or isolated juvenile idiopathic arthritis"; "No cases of SLE". No exclusion was inferred from "one patient (patient X)" statements either, because none names the group. Count-only results (ANA 7/13, CRP, ESR, interferon signature, HLA-B51 and others) were not attributed to anyone.

DEMOGRAPHICS: one family is consanguineous but is not identified, so consanguinity is "not reported" for everyone. Origin (15 Caucasian, 1 Indian, 1 Maghrebian) cannot be attributed to individuals, and recruitment in France was not taken as a country of origin. Sex is stated only for patient 4 ("Her mother") and patient 10 ("His half-brother"), and for relatives through the relation word. Kawasaki disease in patients 7 and 9 is recorded as a feature with its onset age; it came before HA20 onset, so it was not used as age at onset. The ages in figure captions (patient 6 at 14 years, patient 7 at 15 years) are ages at the photograph and the MRI, so they went into severity_or_detail.

CHECKLIST JUDGEMENTS:
- "fever" without any mention of recurrence (half-brother, mother and maternal grandfather of patient 10): "recurrent fever" left "not reported".
- Unspecified "ulcers" or "mucosal ulcers": oral and genital ulcers left "not reported".
- Patient 10's "autoimmune diabetes": mapped to type 1 diabetes.
- Headache in patients 7, 11 and 13: mapped to central nervous system involvement, because the paper calls it "Neurological symptoms". The half-brother's headache was not, because the paper does not describe it that way.
- Patient 1's intestinal lymphoid nodular hyperplasia: not counted as lymphoproliferation.
- Kawasaki disease: not counted as vasculitis.
- Patient 5's necrotic finger lesions: counted as skin lesions (they are reported under cutaneous manifestations).
- Patient 1's endoscopy found "small aphthoid colonic ulcerations" that were "not consistent with IBD or colitis": GI ulcers observed, colitis excluded.
- Patient 10's half-brother, "without documented colitis": colitis recorded as excluded.

VARIANTS:
- Patient 14: Table 3 prints "c. 29T>A; 49A>T" and "p. (Leu10*) p. (Lys17*)". The text prints "c. [29T>A; 49A>T], p. [(Leu10*); p. (Lys17*)]" and calls it a "complex allele". Recorded as one row, with variant type "other".
- Variant type "nonsense" is used only for the stop-gain variants the authors list. The paper's "only one missense variant" is never tied to a patient.
- Transcript NM_006290.4 comes from the Table 3 title.
- No zygosity is stated anywhere.

PRIOR REPORT: patient 16 was reported before (El Khouri et al^44). This goes in publications; source_reference_in_review stays "not reported" because the patient is described first-hand here. Patients 1 and 16 were first labelled PFAPA; this is not recorded as a phenotype.

CONTRADICTIONS IN THE PAPER:
(1) The abstract gives "17 patients from 11 unrelated families"; Results give "11 unrelated, non-consanguineous families and one consanguineous family"; Table 3 lists 12 families.
(2) Median age at diagnosis is "13 years" in the text but "13.5" in Table 1.
(3) The text says "8/17 patients harbouring OTU‐localised mutations", but the Table 3 domain column shows OTU for 15 of 17 patients, and the Discussion gives 58% with OTU nonsense or frameshift variants.
(4) p.Pro457Alafs*16 is called "novel" and also "present in Infevers database", with an Infevers reference in Table 3, which marks only two variants as "Not published" against "Three novel" in the text.
(5) Hepatomegaly is 2/17 on examination against 3/15 on ultrasound (not strictly contradictory).
